albumContext.significance: Studio album featuring ensemble writing with horns and woodwinds; same era as Be-Bop Tango (Roxy and Elsewhere, 1974). Contains Cosmik Debris, Montana, I'm the Slime, Dirty Love, etc. Represents the 'sophisticated pop with polytonal jazz' Zappa style — ensemble composition rather than solo guitar focus.
albumContext.relevanceToSlice: Over-Nite Sensation is the canonical example of Zappa's d4_style_juxtaposition device — doo-wop references (e.g. Dinah-Moe Humm) adjacent to altered jazz harmony. Style juxtaposition at the album macro-level mirrors the bar-level device in the slice.

confirmedHarmonicProgressions.musicalFunction: Chromatic dominant slide — Zappa's signature polytonal juxtaposition at chord-to-chord level
Primary vamp chord on Over-Nite Sensation — most common single chord in songbook. Supports Dorian / minor pentatonic melody.
Suspended dominant — avoids tritone resolution, creates harmonic stasis typical of Zappa non-resolving cadences
Lydian major-7 colour — #11 = Lydian raised 4th, Zappa's preferred major-chord flavour (confirms Little Dots Lydian rule)
Suspended dominant 7ths avoid resolution; used for harmonic suspension rather than ii–V–I drive

characteristicDevices: Cycled 4-note motifs with rhythmic displacement across bars
Polytonal / poly-scale approach over static vamps

synthesisNotes.chordVocabulary: 49 unique chords across 99 pages confirms Zappa's harmonic density. Minor 7th dominance (Am7 26, Bm7 12, Dm7 12, Cm7 9, Em7 8, F#m7 7) reflects the 1973 rock-with-jazz-chords aesthetic. Dominant 7th clusters (C7, D7, Db7, Ab7, Cb7, G7) suggest jazz-influenced accompaniment not common in rock of the era.
synthesisNotes.chromatic7thMotion: C7→Db7 (6 hits) confirmed as a real progression — semitone ascending dominant-7 voice-leading. This mirrors the Pink Napkins C#m7→DM7 semitone root motion and is the clearest OCR-confirmed example of Zappa's chromatic harmonic juxtaposition.
synthesisNotes.lydianConfirmed: Fmaj7#11 (3 hits) directly confirms the Lydian #11 device in the songbook. Combined with Bbmaj7 (4 hits), major-7th chords are consistently decorated with altered upper extensions.
synthesisNotes.suspensionHarmony: B7sus4 (8 hits), C7sus4 (4 hits), Db7sus4 (4 hits) — sus4 dominant 7ths used for non-resolving harmonic stasis rather than functional V→I motion. Confirms 'no ii–V–I chains' rule from fz:d1.
synthesisNotes.flatVIIHarmony: Cb7 (6 hits), Ab7 (8 hits), Db6 (6 hits) — flat-VII and flat-III dominant 7ths common, reinforcing the rock/modal harmonic language layered over jazz voicings.
synthesisNotes.intervalPatternSummary: OCR tab analysis: semitone (44 hits) and minor 3rd (25 hits) dominate — confirms pentatonic + chromatic approach as primary melodic language. Tritone present (2 hits) as dissonance marker.
synthesisNotes.wahPedal: Wah pedal explicitly mentioned 8 times — most of any technique. Aligns with 1973 Zappa solo style (Cosmik Debris, Montana guitar solos).
synthesisNotes.dynamicProfile: f (113) far more frequent than p (23) — louder, more assertive dynamic profile than guitar book. ff appears only 8 times (more sparing than book's 13). fp (5) suggests accent-then-decay gestures.
synthesisNotes.tempoCharacter: 'Moderately' (5 hits) and 'Moderate' (2 hits) dominate — Over-Nite Sensation is mid-tempo ensemble rock, not the extreme fast/slow contrasts of the guitar book solos.
synthesisNotes.keyForSlice: C7→Db7 chromatic slide directly informs fz:d4 (style juxtaposition / chromatic harmonic shift). Am7 as primary vamp chord informs Dorian scale selection for fz:d5. Sus4 dominant chords confirm fz:d1 (no ii–V resolution) at the harmonic level. Fmaj7#11 confirms Lydian #11 colouring available as device.
